notes: Corrected τὰ πολλά: the accepted alignment gave these to the article and many times to the adjective headed on many, which is rule 17's anarthrous generic-noun clause applied where a Greek article stands. Rule 102 governs instead — an article whose complement is a substantival adjective takes both the determiner and the supplied noun, headed on the nominal, and the corpus reads that shape the article's way twelve to none — so τά now takes these … times headed on times and πολλά keeps a bare many.
The demonstrative these is the article's own supplied determiner under rule 60, no Greek demonstrative standing to compete for the slot.
